clue.text: Challenge ministers — it's needed to come clean!

parts.note: to challenge someone is to face or confront them
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy, i.e. ministers of religion

explanation.surface: A rebel defying the clergy is urged to confess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come clean' suggests confessing, but the definition is literal: you need this to wash your face.
explanation.definitionFit: A small towel used for washing is what you need to get yourself clean.

clue.text: This man fared badly when about fifty

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes about, i.e. around, the letter for fifty
something done badly is botched, so the letters of fared are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man did poorly at around fifty years of age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges FARED to AFRED, and 'about' puts L inside it after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, so it can stand for some particular man.

clue.text: Turned out-have to beg in the close

indicators.note: the word for beg is placed in the word for the close

parts.note: the close of something is its end
to sue is to plead or beg, as in sue for peace

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to go begging in a cul-de-sac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a dead-end street; here it means the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that followed or resulted have happened as a consequence.

clue.text: A trial leading to the noose!

indicators.note: the letters of the words A trial lead to, i.e. become, a new word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A court case ends with a hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading to' signals that A TRIAL turns into a different arrangement of its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope with a running loop, a cowboy's noose.

clue.text: The touch-line

parts.note: read not as the edge of a football pitch but literally as a line that just touches a curve

explanation.walkthrough: The touchline marks the side of a rugby or football pitch; in geometry this straight line meets a curve at one point.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry it is a straight line meeting a curve at a single point without crossing it.

clue.text: Receives sound information in actual practice

indicators.note: the receiving phrase is placed in the word for actual

parts.note: actual means real
one who hears takes in information through sound

explanation.surface: Someone takes in genuine guidance while actually practising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receives sound information' reads as a description, but it is simply one who hears; 'in' puts it within the word for actual.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice run before a performance is a run-through.

clue.text: Honest woman with many financial obligations

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name
C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: A truthful woman is saddled with many debts.
explanation.walkthrough: C for 'many' is a crossword convention, from the Roman hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Truthful and accurate, as in a veracious witness.

clue.text: Control the way everything is put back

parts.note: to rein in is to control
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
everything means all

explanation.surface: Restoring order means organising the road so all is replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up again in its place, as with software or fittings.

clue.text: Honour the French dream about

parts.note: rêve is French for dream
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Respect the French ideal of dreaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' tells you to use a French word for dream.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold in deep respect or venerate.

clue.text: Children not being served well

parts.note: a dish that is off is no longer available on the menu
a spring is a natural well or source of water

explanation.surface: Kids are not being properly waited on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like an adverb but is the noun meaning a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Descendants or young, a person's issue.

clue.text: Recover eg in shower

indicators.note: eg is placed in the word for shower

parts.note: a shower is a brief fall of rain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting back on your feet, for example after a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' suggests a bathroom, but it is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To get back something lost, such as possession or strength.

clue.text: A singer who appears less concerned about puff

indicators.note: the word for less concerned goes about, around, the word for puff

parts.note: calmer, more serene
a puff is a piece of publicity, an ad

explanation.surface: A vocalist seems more relaxed about praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puff' suggests breath or smoke, but it is advertising hype; 'about' wraps the comparative of serene around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sings a love song beneath a window at night.

clue.text: The designer exhibiting most odd traits

indicators.note: very strange, so the letters of traits are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: A designer reveals extremely peculiar characteristics.
explanation.definitionFit: A creative person such as a painter or illustrator designs images.

clue.text: Satellites can be so dear it's quite absurd

indicators.note: absurd means nonsensical, so the letters of so dear it's are scrambled

explanation.surface: Satellites cost so much it is ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite absurd' rearranges SO DEAR IT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor planets orbiting the sun, loosely its small satellites.

clue.text: Excessively put out by 10

parts.note: over as a prefix means too much, excessively
the answer to 10 means children, and issue also means children

explanation.surface: Someone is very annoyed by their kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like 'annoyed'; here it means distributed.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue too many shares or banknotes, i.e. to release in excess.

clue.text: Batman taking over?

parts.note: not the superhero but a man with a bat taking his turn when an over begins

explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket; Batman suggests the comic hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the bat-and-ball game who faces overs is a batsman.

clue.text: Consumed something from a terrine

indicators.note: something taken from the words a terrine, i.e. a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone ate a bit of pâté.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of eat, meaning devoured.

clue.text: She's in the lead always

indicators.note: the woman is found in the run of letters of lead always

explanation.surface: She's always the front-runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She's' gives the definition and the indicator: She has in.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for some particular female.

clue.text: Note the craft shown in a letter

parts.note: E is a musical note
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: The ship is mentioned in a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt-out name of the nineteenth character of the alphabet.

clue.text: Deserve to be broken up-split

indicators.note: something broken up is in pieces, so the letters of Deserve are rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple deserves to separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut off or divided completely.

clue.text: A winger is main dupe

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
to gull is to dupe or trick

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing is the chief fall guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a wide football player; here it is anything with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal bird, a creature with wings.

clue.text: A nincompoop when taking direction

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left
S is south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A fool takes orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey, figuratively a stupid person.

clue.text: Watch and call when there's a leak

parts.note: to watch is to see
to page someone is to call them

explanation.surface: Keep an eye out and phone the plumber if water escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid slowly escaping or trickling through.

clue.text: Supplement written in for by Ben, Richard, and John

indicators.note: the word is written inside the words Ben, Richard

explanation.surface: A supplement drafted for a joint byline of three authors.
explanation.definitionFit: To add to and improve, making richer.

clue.text: Conditions in America

definitions.meaning: situations or circumstances one is in
the US is often called the ...

explanation.definitionFit: Circumstances are one sense; the USA, colloquially, is the other.

clue.text: 21 will get possibly ten to acquiesce

parts.note: the answer to 21 across, a fool

indicators.note: possibly signals that ten might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A fool will be persuaded by around ten to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TEN to ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement or consent, to give one's assent.

clue.text: Picture a man bound up with business

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: a serf was a man bound to the land
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: Imagine a man tied up in his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SERF into FRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting made on wet plaster, a type of picture.

clue.text: Personal treatment for depression is test

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
to try is to test

explanation.surface: Therapy for depression is a personal test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' looks like an illness; it is a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental care is treatment given to one person's teeth.

clue.text: A native in bed?

parts.note: a native here is a farmed shellfish of British waters, which lives in a bed on the seabed

explanation.walkthrough: Natives are a British name for home-grown oysters raised in oyster beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivalve shellfish raised in a bed and sold as a native.

clue.text: The comprehensive principle pains them dreadfully

indicators.note: done dreadfully means badly, so the letters of pains them are jumbled

explanation.surface: An all-embracing doctrine causes them dreadful pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The belief that God is identical with the universe, an all-embracing doctrine.

clue.text: Soaks having to perform exercises

parts.note: to do is to perform
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Drunks have to do their workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soaks' suggests drunkards; here it is a verb meaning drenches.
explanation.definitionFit: Drenches with water.

clue.text: Stopping canoeists going wrong

indicators.note: going wrong means going awry, so the letters of canoeists are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paddlers halting because things went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A coming to an end, halting.
